title: Fun and relaxing with some performance issues
body: I have used Finch for about half a year now. This is a great app for a fun and relaxing self care list. It is engaging to take care of your bird and to keep up with the list, without feeling like you have to spend a bunch of time in the app every day! The free version works well enough, and there are very few annoying upgrade prompts. The only drawback is some performance issues. I have an iPhone 11 Pro so it’s a bit older and the app does crash sometimes, usually when doing something that requires a lot of graphics such as sending a vibe to a friend or going on an adventure. My progress isnt lost in the crashes, but it is annoying to restart the app considering it happens at least a couple times per week. I probably wouldn’t have upgraded anyway, but with the performance problems I really feel I would not spend the money on a paid subscription. However I will continue to use the app, and I would recommend trying it especially if you have a newer phone.

title: Surprisingly broad
body: I’ve heard very good things about this app and I finally decided to give it a try. Very glad that I did! It’s only been a few days to be fair, but it’s already proven to be a very anchoring, comforting and encouraging little thing in my life. I’m surprised with how much it has to offer, without it feeling pushy or lacking at the same time. I like it a lot. I try over and over to make schedules and stuff for myself to stick to, but always let them slip away sooner or later (usually sooner). This app feels rewarding with just that little pat on the back, and gives me something to look forward to even when it’s really just me doing things for myself. It’s a nice tool. Again, I’m surprised at the different categories there are to goals, features things like the mood tracker, the ability to write little journal entries and so on. This app makes me think a bit further about how I’m actually doing and about the various things I could do for myself to improve that, whether improving would concern my mood, activity, productivity, health, social life or state of mind... Etc! It’s charming that you can add friends on here and have joint goals, but even just having your little pet feels social in a way too, which is nice. I guess I didn’t know how nice words of encouragement from a cartoon bird could be. Thanks a lot Finch! I’m really enjoying this so far, it motivates me enough to do the little things, which get the ball rolling for the bigger things (but - also remind me that it’s okay to take it easy.) ! Super 👏🙏🖤❤️

title: The best self-care app I’ve tried
body: I’ve heard of Finch for a long time, but I didn’t want to download it because I didn’t think that a silly game would help me with self-care needs. Yet, one day for some reason I downloaded it and I realized how wrong I was. The app is really well thought out based on best practices in self-care and really considers the users’s needs. For example, you can stay on top of daily self-care goals like meditation and self affirmations by creating a recurring goal that shows up on your list every day then you can link it to the many meditation and affirmations  they have available so you can do these exercise exercises in just a few taps. For goals that are harder for you to complete. They also have ways to incentivize you to complete them. There are also small things that greatly help, such as being able to customize a goal to occur  every day, week, month, etc, or having it carryover to the next day. It’s like a project management software for self care. Overall, this app helps you build good habits as it helps you build more positive associations with self-care habits. This is the only self-care app where I have been able to login every day consistently and look forward to using.  I really really really recommend this app.

title: Good Vibes and Inclusion for All!🐥
body:
I once used this app in the past, and I loved its early version even then.
So when my mental health tanked yet again while I couldn’t get my medication increased I turned to it just to see if it could get me through it.
The program for guardianships to those who can’t afford to pay for premium is something I hope to contribute to one when I can afford it🥰
The premium I seem to have been lucky enough to receive makes the app incredibly comforting and helpful!

This app is the only place where I don’t feel weird about my sexuality or gender. Like the reality of what they mean to people doesn’t matter when it’s just you and your birb.

Somehow it’s not just an app, it’s making the bad days feel okay.
My only wish is that you could have the option to put in your mental health diagnoses (autism, transgender, imposter syndrome, ocd, adhd, all the big guns you’d expect to see) so that they could get an understanding of what reflection topics could be added in the future.

But everything else is beyond compare! Seeing as when my mental health is bad I struggle to actually get help, this app is really kind in that I don’t have to put myself through expenses and stress just to get some thoughts off my chest.❤️
(in the updates since I last used the app I especially love all the inclusive flags and language added even if I don’t use them all they reassures me it’s a safe space for everyone)

Thank you all that work on this project!

title: At first, a fun way to practice self-care. Now, it's just a chore.
body:
I started using this app a couple months ago, in the beginning of November I believe. I had a blast! I could set goals for the day and I could send off my bird to talk to my friends. It was great, and I think it helped me.

But after a few months of using it, it's just turned into a chore. I do it every day right before bed because I haven't bothered checking in throughout the day. It doesn't help me, it just feels like a tool that collects information about my mood, which further makes me feel bad, because it's almost all negative.

The events are an interesting feature. They're a great incentive to check off some goals every day, so you get daily rewards tied to the current month. But you'd better not forget to claim those rewards before the end of the month, else you lose everything you didn't claim. And did I mention it takes an unreasonable amount of time to go into the event menu, find the item you want to claim, claim it, then specify that you don't want to sell it nor equip it? It takes longer than it needs to, especially when you have a bit of a backlog of them.

Finch was a decent app for me, at first. But now, it's lost its luster for me. I can recommend it for people who really need help with self-care and don't have problems with procrastinating, but not for anyone else.
